aboutText:
I am a computational chemist specializing in molecular dynamics, nanomaterials, and computational mechanics.
 My work focuses on understanding the nano-mechanical behavior of materials, exploring structure-property relationships, and applying atomistic simulations to solve complex challenges.

education.description:
Conducting computational research on stress-, shear-, and compression-induced phase transformations in silicon and amorphous ice.
- Investigating atomistic mechanisms of polymorphic transformations, amorphization, and crystallization using molecular dynamics simulations.
- Examining how stress state, strain rate, crystallographic orientation, and nanoscale confinement govern transformation pathways.
- Developing structural-analysis workflows using LAMMPS, OVITO, Python, ASE, DScribe, and machine-learning-based atomic descriptors.
Focused heavily on computational modeling and stress simulations for structural engineering.

education.institution: Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET)
education.description: Graduated with honors. Completed a capstone project on the stability of 2D layered materials.

roles.title: Research Assistant (Chemistry & Mechanical Engineering)
roles.description:
Conducted extensive research exploring nanoconfinement and structure-property relationships in subsurface environments.
- Developed computational models for complex material simulations.
- Performed molecular dynamics simulations to analyze atomic behavior.
- Authored comprehensive technical papers based on simulation outcomes.

roles.title: Course Teaching Assistant (Chemistry)
roles.description:
Taught undergraduate courses on Thermodynamics and Physical Chemistry.
- Led laboratory sessions and managed lab safety protocols.
- Graded assignments and provided extensive mentorship during office hours.

roles.title: Laboratory Teaching Assistant (Mech Eng.)
roles.description:
Lab Teaching Assistant for ME EN 3315 (Mechanics of Materials).
- Assisted Professors: Dr. Michael Czabaj, Dr. Bozo Vazic, Dr. Ken Monson, Dr. Owen Kingstedt.
- Guided students through complex mechanical testing protocols.

roles.title: Undergraduate Researcher
roles.description:
Investigated atomistic reaction mechanisms of CVD-grown 2D materials.
- Analyzed the effects of substrate structures on hexagonal boron nitride.
- Contributed to publications regarding mechanical stability and material properties.

roles.title: Design Engineer
roles.description:
Designed LPG Spherical storage tanks, Cylindrical storage tanks, Ball valves, and Actuated valves.
- Designed P&ID of LPG network, Fire fighting network, and Industrial air network.
- Executed 3D Pipe Routing of different LPG Plants using AutoCAD Plant 3D and SOLIDWORKS Pipe Routing.
- Designed Land Layouts of different LPG Plants using AutoCAD and created sample P&IDs using Microsoft Visio.

roles.description:
Maintained machinery and assisted students with their academic projects.
- Managed fabrication of 13 undergraduate thesis projects, 1000 key rings, and 10+ intricate designs.
- Operated CNC milling machines, laser cutters, and 3D printers while ensuring optimal lab instrument functionality.

journals.mla: Arafat, Abdullah, et al. "Atomistic reaction mechanism of CVD grown MoS2 through MoO3 and H2S precursors." Scientific Reports, vol. 12, no. 1, 2022, p. 16085.
journals.preview: This paper details a theoretical model for the chemical vapor deposition of MoS2, exploring intermediary transition states and calculating activation energies for the reaction pathways using atomistic simulations.

journals.mla: Komol, M.M.R., A.K. Podder, Abdullah Arafat, and T. Nabeed. "Remote sensing global ranged door lock security system via mobile communication." International Journal of Wireless and Microwave Technologies, vol. 9, no. 5, 2019, pp. 25-37.
journals.preview: A novel approach to global ranged security utilizing mobile communication modules integrated with electromechanical systems for real-time authentication and access control.

journals.mla: Ak, İ., H. Adin, Abdullah Arafat, and M. Okumuş. "Mechanical properties of Cu-Ni alloys: Comparison of experimental and MD simulation approaches." Physica B: Condensed Matter, vol. 700, 2025, p. 416928.
journals.preview: Investigates the tensile strength and elasticity of Cu-Ni alloys, drawing direct correlations between laboratory experimental data and simulated molecular dynamics predictions to validate computational models.

journals.mla: Sarkar, M.M.H., M.S. Islam, Abdullah Arafat, A.S.M.J. Islam, and N. Ferdous. "Effects of the substrate structure on the CVD growth of two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride." The Journal of Physical Chemistry C, vol. 126, no. 14, 2022, pp. 6373-6384.
journals.preview: Focuses on the epitaxial growth mechanics of h-BN, demonstrating how differing substrate lattice structures influence the orientation, defect rate, and quality of the resulting 2D material.

journals.mla: Sajal, W.R., et al., including Abdullah Arafat. "Molecular dynamics study of mechanical stability of Ti4C3 MXene subjected to chirality, temperature, strain rate, and point-vacancy for Lithium-ion batteries." Heliyon, vol. 10, no. 19, 2024.
journals.preview: A comprehensive analysis of how extreme conditions and structural defects impact the durability of MXene materials, specifically aiming to improve longevity in Lithium-ion battery applications.
